Metadata.title: Fileflect — Convert files and images for free
Metadata.description: Convert images and documents with no watermarks and no sign-up. Whatever can be done on your device stays there.

HomePage.title: Convert your files without them ever leaving your computer
HomePage.tagline: Images and PDFs are processed right in your browser: faster, more private and free. No watermarks, no account needed.

privacy.title: Actually private
privacy.body: Your images and PDFs are never uploaded — everything happens on your device.

speed.title: Seriously fast
speed.body: No waiting for uploads or downloads. Conversion starts instantly.

free.title: Free, no sign-up
free.body: No watermarks, no mandatory accounts and no hidden limits.

office.title: Office documents too
office.body: Word, Excel and PowerPoint are converted on our server and deleted within 1 hour.

HomePage.badge: Your files never leave your device

how.heading: How it works
how.subtitle: Three steps, nothing to install and no account needed.

drop.title: Drop your file
drop.body: Drop images or PDFs on the area above, or tap it to pick them. You can add several at once.

pick.title: Pick a format
pick.body: Choose the output format and, if you like, adjust the quality or size.

download.title: Download the result
download.body: The conversion runs on your device in seconds. Download each file or all of them in a ZIP.

free.a: Yes. You can convert without paying, without an account and without watermarks. The Pro plan is optional: it removes ads and raises the limits.

upload.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
upload.a: Images and PDFs are processed right in your browser and never leave your device. Only office documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) are converted on our server, and they are deleted within 1 hour.

formats.a: JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO, HEIC and SVG images; tools to merge, split, rotate, organize and compress PDFs; images to PDF and PDF to image; and Word, Excel and PowerPoint documents to PDF.

mobile.q: Does it work on my phone?
mobile.a: Yes. Fileflect works in your phone or tablet browser, with no app to install. For example, you can turn iPhone HEIC photos into JPG.

batch.q: Can I convert several files at once?
batch.a: Yes. Add several files at once and download them one by one or all together in a ZIP file.

quality.a: You decide: you can adjust the quality of compressed formats (JPG, WEBP, AVIF). Lossless formats such as PNG keep the image exactly as it is.

merge-pdf.title: Merge PDF
merge-pdf.description: Combine several PDFs into one, in any order. Your files are never uploaded.
merge-pdf.about: Merge PDF joins several documents into a single file. You can change the order with the move up and move down buttons before merging. Pages are copied as they are: text, links and image quality don't change.

faq.q1: Do I lose quality when merging PDFs?
faq.a1: No. Pages are copied without being recompressed, so text stays selectable and images keep their resolution.
faq.q2: Can I choose the order of the files?
faq.a2: Yes. Use each file's move up and move down buttons; the final PDF follows the order of the list.
faq.q3: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?
faq.a3: No. An encrypted PDF can't be read without its password; you'll see a warning and can remove it from the list.

split-pdf.title: Split PDF
split-pdf.description: Split a PDF into several files or extract just the pages you need.
split-pdf.about: Split PDF separates a document into several files. You can save each page as its own PDF, make one PDF per range (for example 1-3, 4-6) or extract just some pages into a single file. When the result has several PDFs, they download together as a ZIP.

faq.q1: How do I write page ranges?
faq.a1: Separate ranges with commas: 1-3, 5, 8-. A single number is one page and "8-" means from page 8 to the end.
faq.q2: Can I take out just a few pages without splitting everything?
faq.a2: Yes. Choose "Extract pages into one PDF" and type the pages you want to keep.
faq.q3: Is the original PDF changed?
faq.a3: No. Fileflect creates new files and your original PDF stays the same on your device.

rotate-pdf.title: Rotate PDF
rotate-pdf.description: Turn the pages of a PDF and save it the right way up.
rotate-pdf.about: Rotate PDF turns pages 90° clockwise, 90° counterclockwise or 180°. You can rotate every page or only the ones you list, such as scanned pages that came out upside down. The rotation is saved in the file, so it looks right in any reader.

faq.q1: Can I rotate only some pages?
faq.a1: Yes. Choose "Only some" and type the pages or ranges, for example 2, 5-7.
faq.q2: Does rotating a PDF reduce quality?
faq.a2: No. Only the page orientation changes; the content isn't recompressed.
faq.q3: Does the rotation stay when I open it in another app?
faq.a3: Yes. The rotation is saved in the PDF and is respected by Acrobat, web browsers and phone readers.

organize-pdf.title: Organize PDF pages
organize-pdf.description: Reorder, rotate or delete PDF pages with thumbnails.
organize-pdf.about: Organize PDF shows a thumbnail of every page so you can rearrange the document visually: drag pages to their new place (or use the buttons), rotate the ones that need it and delete the ones you don't want. When you're done, you download a new PDF in the chosen order.

faq.q1: Can I use it without a mouse?
faq.a1: Yes. Each page has buttons to move it earlier or later, rotate it and delete it, usable with the keyboard and on touch screens.
faq.q2: I deleted a page by mistake. Can I get it back?
faq.a2: Yes. The "Restore all" button brings back the original document before you download.
faq.q3: Does it work with long PDFs?
faq.a3: Yes, although thumbnails take longer to generate for long or image-heavy documents, especially on phones.

images-to-pdf.title: Images to PDF
images-to-pdf.description: Turn JPG, PNG, HEIC and other photos into a single PDF.
images-to-pdf.about: Images to PDF creates a document with one image per page. It accepts JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF, ICO, HEIC (iPhone photos) and SVG. You can reorder the images, choose the page size (same as the image, A4 or Letter) and a margin; photos are turned according to their EXIF orientation.

faq.q1: Can I turn iPhone photos (HEIC) into a PDF?
faq.a1: Yes. HEIC photos are decoded in your browser and added to the PDF like any other image.
faq.q2: Which page size should I pick?
faq.a2: "Same as image" adds no borders. A4 or Letter are good for printing or sending documents: the image is centered and fitted without stretching.
faq.q3: What if an image is damaged?
faq.a3: You'll see a warning with the name of the file that failed so you can remove or replace it; your other images are kept.

compress-pdf.title: Compress PDF
compress-pdf.description: Make your PDFs smaller to send them by email or WhatsApp.
compress-pdf.about: Compress PDF makes the file smaller by re-encoding the photos inside it, which are usually why a PDF is heavy. Text, fonts and vector drawings are kept as they are. There are three levels: low (best quality), recommended and strong (smallest file).

faq.q1: Why did my PDF barely shrink?
faq.a1: If the PDF is mostly text, or its images are already optimized, there's little to reduce. In that case Fileflect tells you instead of giving you a bigger file.
faq.a2: No. Only images are recompressed; text stays sharp, selectable and searchable.
faq.q3: Which level should I pick for email or WhatsApp?
faq.a3: Recommended is usually enough. If the file is still large, try strong: photos lose some detail but the document stays readable.

json-to-csv.title: JSON to CSV
json-to-csv.description: Convert JSON into a CSV or TSV table for Excel or Google Sheets. Your data is never uploaded.
json-to-csv.about: JSON to CSV turns a list of JSON objects into a table: each object becomes a row and each key a column. Nested objects become dotted columns (for example address.city) and lists become numbered columns (tags.0, tags.1). Choose comma, semicolon or tab (TSV), and add the UTF-8 mark so Excel shows accented characters correctly.

faq.q1: Which JSON does it accept?
faq.a1: A list of objects, a single object, an object wrapping a single list (like '{'"items": [...]'}') or a list of lists, which is written as rows as is. If the JSON has a syntax error you will see a warning.
faq.q2: Why does Excel show broken accents or everything in one column?
faq.a2: Keep the Excel-compatible option checked (it adds the UTF-8 mark). If your Excel uses a comma as the decimal separator, as in much of Europe and Latin America, choose semicolon.
faq.q3: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a3: No. The conversion runs in your browser, in the background, and the file never leaves your device.

csv-to-json.title: CSV to JSON
csv-to-json.description: Convert CSV or TSV into JSON with automatic delimiter detection. Your data is never uploaded.
csv-to-json.about: CSV to JSON reads a table with a header row and produces a list of JSON objects, one per row. It detects whether the file uses commas, semicolons, tabs or pipes, keeps quotes and line breaks inside cells, and reads files saved by Excel in UTF-8 or Windows-1252. Optionally it converts numbers and true/false, and rebuilds objects from dotted columns.

faq.q1: How are numbers handled?
faq.a1: With value conversion on, a number is written as a number only if it reads back the same: 007 or a 20-digit number stay as text so no zeros or precision are lost. Empty cells become null.
faq.q2: What about empty or repeated headers?
faq.a2: They get a name of their own (column3, name_2) so no column is lost. Rows with fewer cells are filled with null.
faq.q3: Can I get nested objects?
faq.a3: Yes. Columns like address.city or tags.0 become objects and lists. If a column clashes with another one, it is kept as is so no data is lost.

json-to-yaml.title: JSON to YAML
json-to-yaml.description: Convert JSON into readable YAML for config files, Kubernetes or CI. In your browser.
json-to-yaml.about: JSON to YAML rewrites your JSON data as block-indented YAML, easier to read and edit by hand in config files, Kubernetes manifests, docker-compose files or CI pipelines. Strings an older YAML reader would take as something else (yes, no, on, 007, dates) are quoted so they keep their type.

faq.q1: Why are some values quoted?
faq.a1: Because without quotes some YAML 1.1 readers would read them differently: yes and on as true, 007 as a number or 2020-01-01 as a date. Quotes make sure they stay text.
faq.a2: Yes. Keys keep their order, and numbers, booleans and null are written with their YAML type. Long lines are not wrapped.
faq.q3: Can I convert several files at once?
faq.a3: Yes. Pick several .json files and download each YAML separately or all of them in a ZIP.

yaml-to-json.title: YAML to JSON
yaml-to-json.description: Convert YAML (including multiple documents and anchors) into valid JSON. Your files are never uploaded.
yaml-to-json.about: YAML to JSON reads YAML 1.2 files, including ones with several documents separated by ---, anchors and aliases, and merge keys (<<) like those in docker-compose or GitLab CI, and produces indented JSON. Several documents become a list. Custom tags are never executed: they are read as text.

faq.q1: Is it safe to open an unknown YAML file?
faq.a1: Yes. No code runs, and files with too many aliases, which can multiply their size until the device freezes (the billion laughs attack), are rejected with a warning.
faq.a2: Because in YAML 1.2, the current standard, only true and false are booleans. Likewise, dates stay as text in the JSON.
faq.q3: What if there are repeated keys or a syntax error?
faq.a3: You will see a warning instead of an incomplete JSON: a repeated key in the same object is an error in YAML.

json-to-toml.title: JSON to TOML
json-to-toml.description: Convert JSON into TOML for config files like pyproject.toml or Cargo.toml. In your browser.
json-to-toml.about: JSON to TOML turns a JSON object into a TOML file with tables ([section]) and arrays of tables ([[items]]), the config format of tools like Cargo, Poetry, Hugo or pyproject.toml. Keys with spaces or symbols are quoted.

faq.q1: Which JSON can be converted?
faq.a1: An object at the root. TOML doesn't allow a list or a bare value as a document: in that case you will see a warning explaining it.
faq.a2: TOML has no null: keys set to null are left out. A null inside a list can't be represented and you will see a warning.
faq.q3: Is any information lost?
faq.a3: Apart from nulls, no: strings, numbers, booleans, lists and nested objects are kept, and the TOML reads back the same.

toml-to-json.title: TOML to JSON
toml-to-json.description: Convert TOML files (Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, config.toml) into JSON. Your files are never uploaded.
toml-to-json.about: TOML to JSON reads TOML 1.0 files with tables, inline tables, arrays of tables and dates, and produces indented JSON. Use it to process a project's configuration with tools that only understand JSON, or to review its structure.

faq.q1: How are dates converted?
faq.a1: As ISO 8601 text: a date-time becomes 1979-05-27T07:32:00.000Z and a plain date 1979-05-27.
faq.a2: JSON in the browser can't hold integers above 2^53 without losing precision, so such a file is rejected with a warning instead of changing the value.
faq.q3: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a3: No. The conversion runs in your browser and the file never leaves your device.

json-to-xml.title: JSON to XML
json-to-xml.description: Convert JSON into a valid, indented XML document, attributes included. In your browser.
json-to-xml.about: JSON to XML builds a well-formed XML document from your JSON data. Keys starting with @ are written as attributes and #text as the element's text; lists become repeated elements. If the JSON has a single key at the root, that key is the root element; otherwise everything goes inside '<root>'.

faq.q1: What about keys that aren't valid XML names?
faq.a1: They are fixed so the XML stays valid: spaces and symbols become underscores (my key → my_key) and a name starting with a digit gets a leading underscore.
faq.a2: Use keys starting with @: '{"book": {"@id": "1", "title": "Dune"}}' produces '<book id="1"><title>Dune</title></book>'.
faq.q3: Are special characters escaped?
faq.a3: Yes. &, '< and >' in text and quotes in attributes are written as entities, so the result is always valid XML.

xml-to-json.title: XML to JSON
xml-to-json.description: Convert XML into JSON with attributes, repeated elements and CDATA. Safe against XXE, and your files are never uploaded.
xml-to-json.about: XML to JSON reads XML documents and turns them into JSON: each element is a key, attributes get a leading @, repeated elements form a list and CDATA content is kept as text. Values stay text, because XML has no types: 007 stays 007.

faq.q1: Is it safe to open an unknown XML file?
faq.a1: Yes. Documents that declare entities ('<!ENTITY>'), the way in for attacks like XXE or billion laughs, are refused with a warning before reading, and nothing is fetched from the internet.
faq.a2: Because in XML everything is text, and guessing types could change data (leading zeros, codes). This way you get exactly what the file says.
faq.q3: Are comments kept?
faq.a3: No. Comments and processing instructions have no JSON equivalent and are left out; the rest of the content is kept.

json-formatter.title: JSON formatter and validator
json-formatter.description: Validate your JSON, see the line and column of the error, and pretty-print or minify it.
json-formatter.about: The JSON formatter checks that your JSON is valid and, if it is, rewrites it indented with 2 or 4 spaces or tabs, or minifies it into a single line to save space. If there is an error, it tells you the line and column, for example an extra comma before a closing brace. It can also sort keys alphabetically to compare files.

faq.q1: How do I find the error in my JSON?
faq.a1: When formatting, the warning shows the line and column of the first problem. The most common ones are trailing commas, single quotes instead of double quotes and unquoted keys.
faq.a2: No. It only removes spaces and line breaks; values, order and types stay the same.
faq.q3: What is sorting keys for?
faq.a3: To compare two files with the same keys in a different order, or to get cleaner diffs in version control. Lists keep their order.

xml-formatter.title: XML formatter and validator
xml-formatter.description: Validate your XML, see the line and column of the error, and pretty-print or minify it.
xml-formatter.about: The XML formatter checks that the document is well-formed (closed tags, quoted attributes) and rewrites it indented or minified. Comments, CDATA sections, attributes and references like & are kept as they were. If there is an error, it shows the line and column.

faq.q1: Which errors does it find?
faq.a1: Unclosed or badly nested tags, repeated or unquoted attributes, and characters that aren't allowed. It is a well-formedness check: it does not validate against an XSD or DTD schema.
faq.a2: Whitespace between tags is replaced by the new indentation, and the DOCTYPE declaration is left out. Content, comments and CDATA are kept.
faq.q3: Is it safe with unknown files?
faq.a3: Yes. Documents that declare entities (the way in for XXE attacks) are refused with a warning, and nothing is fetched from the internet.

yaml-formatter.title: YAML formatter and validator
yaml-formatter.description: Validate your YAML, see the line and column of the error, and re-indent it keeping comments.
yaml-formatter.about: The YAML formatter validates config files such as docker-compose, Kubernetes or CI pipelines and re-indents them evenly with 2 or 4 spaces. It keeps comments, anchors and every document separated by ---. If there is a syntax error or a repeated key, it shows the line and column.

faq.q1: Why is there no tab option?
faq.a1: Because YAML doesn't allow tabs for indentation: a file indented with tabs is not valid.
faq.a2: Yes. Full-line and end-of-line comments are kept, as are anchors and aliases.
faq.q3: Does it catch repeated keys?
faq.a3: Yes. A repeated key at the same level is an error in YAML, and many programs silently take the last one; here you get a warning with its position.

base64-encode.title: Base64 encode
base64-encode.description: Turn text or any file into Base64 or a data URL to embed it in HTML, CSS or JSON.
base64-encode.about: Base64 encode turns text (as UTF-8) or the bytes of any file (image, PDF, font) into Base64 text, the format used to embed files in HTML, CSS, JSON or email. Get plain Base64, wrapped every 76 characters as email expects, or a data URL ready for a src attribute.

faq.q1: How big is the result?
faq.a1: Base64 is about 33% larger than the original file: every 3 bytes are written as 4 characters.
faq.a2: No. It is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can decode it. Don't use it to protect passwords or private information.
faq.q3: What is a data URL?
faq.a3: It is the Base64 preceded by the file type, like data:image/png;base64,…, and it can be used directly as an image src or in CSS.

base64-decode.title: Base64 decode
base64-decode.description: Turn Base64 or a data URL back into the original text or file, with its type detected.
base64-decode.about: Base64 decode recovers the original bytes from Base64 text or a data URL and gives you the file to download. It detects the type from the data URL or the content (PNG, JPG, PDF and more) and picks the extension; if the result is text, it is shown so you can copy it. Line breaks, the URL-safe alphabet (- and _) and missing = padding are accepted.

faq.q1: How do I know which file was inside?
faq.a1: If the Base64 comes in a data URL, its declared type is used; otherwise it is recognized from the content. If it can't be recognized, it downloads as .bin with the exact bytes.
faq.q2: Why does it say it isn't valid Base64?
faq.a2: Because it contains characters outside the Base64 alphabet or a piece is missing. Check that you copied all of it.
faq.q3: Is the decoded file identical to the original?
faq.a3: Yes, byte for byte. Decoding doesn't recompress or change anything.

url-encode.title: URL encode and decode
url-encode.description: Encode text for use in a URL (%20, %C3%B1) or decode a URL back into readable text.
url-encode.about: URL encode turns spaces, accents and symbols into percent sequences (for example ñ becomes %C3%B1) so they can be used safely in links and parameters. Encode a value, which also escapes / ? & and =, or a whole URL, which keeps them. Decode mode does the opposite and can read + as a space, as in web forms.

faq.q1: What's the difference between a value and a whole URL?
faq.a1: For a parameter, such as search text, & = ? and / must be escaped so they don't break the URL. In a whole URL those characters have a role and are kept as they are.
faq.a2: Web forms send spaces as +. Uncheck the option if + means a plus sign in your text.
faq.q3: What about a malformed %?
faq.a3: You will see a warning: a sequence like %E0%A4%A is incomplete and doesn't stand for any character.

hash-generator.title: MD5 and SHA hash generator
hash-generator.description: Calculate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 of text or files and verify a checksum.
hash-generator.about: The hash generator calculates MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 checksums of text (as UTF-8) or of any file without uploading it: files are read in parts in your browser, so large files work too. Paste the hash published by whoever distributes a file to check that your download is complete and has not been altered. The result downloads as checksums.txt in the format sha256sum -c reads.

faq.q1: How do I check that a download is not damaged?
faq.a1: Choose the file, paste the checksum from the official site into “Expected hash” and calculate. You will see whether it matches and with which algorithm; it is recognized by its length.
faq.a2: SHA-256 or SHA-512. MD5 and SHA-1 catch download errors, but they are no longer safe against someone deliberately crafting files with the same hash.
faq.q3: Can a hash be used to store passwords?
faq.a3: Not directly: passwords need slow, salted functions such as bcrypt or Argon2. Fast hashes like these are for verifying files and integrity.

uuid-generator.title: UUID generator
uuid-generator.description: Generate random v4 or time-ordered v7 UUIDs, one or in bulk, with or without hyphens.
uuid-generator.about: The UUID generator creates unique identifiers following RFC 9562 with your browser's cryptographic random generator. Version 4 is fully random; version 7 starts with the date and time in milliseconds, so the identifiers sort by creation time, which is handy as a primary key in databases. You can generate up to 10,000 at once, in upper case or without hyphens, and download them as text.

faq.q1: Can two UUIDs be the same?
faq.a1: Not in practice: a v4 UUID has 122 random bits, so the chance of a repeat is negligible even after billions of them.
faq.a2: When the identifiers are database keys: since they are ordered by time, indexes fragment less than with v4 UUIDs. Keep in mind that they reveal when they were created.
faq.q3: Are the generated UUIDs stored?
faq.a3: No. They are generated in your browser and never sent to a server.

timestamp-converter.title: Unix timestamp converter
timestamp-converter.description: Convert Unix timestamps in seconds or milliseconds to date and time in any time zone, and dates to timestamps.
timestamp-converter.about: The timestamp converter turns Unix timestamps (seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds) into readable dates and dates into timestamps. Paste one per line: it detects the unit from the number of digits and also accepts ISO 8601 dates (2023-11-14T22:13:20Z) or email-style dates (RFC 2822). For each line you get the seconds, the milliseconds, the date in UTC and the time in the time zone you choose, with its UTC offset and daylight saving time applied.

faq.q1: How does it know whether a number is in seconds or milliseconds?
faq.a1: From the number of digits: up to 11 is seconds, up to 14 milliseconds, up to 17 microseconds and more is nanoseconds. If your data differs, choose the unit yourself.
faq.q2: Which zone is used for a date without a time zone?
faq.a2: The zone chosen in the selector. If the date includes Z or an offset such as -03:00, that one is used.
faq.q3: What about daylight saving time?
faq.a3: It is applied with your browser's time zone database. If a local time happens twice when clocks go back, the first one is used.

qr-generator.title: QR code generator
qr-generator.description: Create QR codes for text, links, Wi-Fi networks or contacts and download them as PNG or SVG.
qr-generator.about: The QR code generator turns text, a link, Wi-Fi network details or a contact card (vCard) into a code any phone reads with its camera. Choose the size, the error correction level and the colors, then download it as PNG to use right away or as SVG to print at any size without losing sharpness. The code never expires and doesn't go through a link shortener: it holds your data directly.

faq.q1: Does the QR code stop working over time?
faq.a1: No. The data is inside the code itself, with no redirects or services in between, so it works as long as the image can be read.
faq.q2: Which error correction level should I choose?
faq.a2: Medium works for almost everything. Use a higher level if the code is printed on surfaces that can get scratched or stained; it uses more modules, so the code looks denser.
faq.q3: How do I share my Wi-Fi with a QR code?
faq.a3: Choose Wi-Fi and enter the network name and password with the same security type your router uses. When scanned, Android and iPhone offer to join without typing the password.

qr-reader.title: Read a QR code from an image
qr-reader.description: Read the content of a QR code in a photo or screenshot, without using the camera.
qr-reader.about: The QR code reader finds the code in a photo or screenshot (PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF, BMP or AVIF) and shows its content so you can copy it: a link, text, Wi-Fi details or a contact. It also reads light codes on dark backgrounds and tries several scales to find small codes in large photos. The image is analyzed in your browser.

faq.q1: Why can't it find the code in my photo?
faq.a1: Usually the photo is blurry, taken at a steep angle, or the code is cut off. Crop the image around the code or take the photo straight on in good light.
faq.q2: Does it open the link automatically?
faq.a2: No. It only shows the content, so you can check where a link goes before opening it.
faq.q3: Can it read several codes at once?
faq.a3: You can choose several images and get the content of each; one code is read from each image.

password-generator.title: Password generator
password-generator.description: Create strong random passwords with the length and characters you choose.
password-generator.about: The password generator creates random passwords with your browser's cryptographic random generator, without bias: every character is equally likely. Choose the length, whether to use upper case, lower case, numbers and symbols, and whether to avoid look-alike characters such as l, 1, O and 0. Every password includes at least one character of each chosen type, and you'll see its strength in bits of entropy.

faq.q1: How long should a password be?
faq.a1: At least 16 characters with letters, numbers and symbols (about 100 bits). For the master password of a password manager, 20 or more is better.
faq.q2: Do you store or see the passwords I generate?
faq.a2: No. They are generated in your browser and never sent to a server. Close the tab when you're done.
faq.q3: What do bits of entropy mean?
faq.a3: They measure how many guesses it would take: each bit doubles the number. From 80 bits on, a random password withstands brute-force attacks even offline.

word-counter.title: Word and character counter
word-counter.description: Count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs as you type, and switch text to upper or lower case.
word-counter.about: The word counter instantly shows how many words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences, paragraphs and lines your text has, plus an estimated reading time. It counts characters as they appear, so an emoji or an accented letter counts as one, and it finds words in Chinese too, which has no spaces. You can also switch the text to UPPER CASE, lower case, Title Case or Sentence case, copy it or download it.

faq.q1: Does it count like Word or Google Docs?
faq.a1: Almost always. Hyphenated words or numbers with commas may differ, because each program applies its own rules; this one uses the Unicode rules for the page's language.
faq.a2: Yes: open a text file (.txt, .md, .csv, .srt…) and it loads into the box. If it comes from Windows with accents in another encoding, that is detected automatically.
faq.q3: How is the reading time calculated?
faq.a3: At 200 words per minute, rounded up.

color-converter.title: Color converter
color-converter.description: Convert colors between HEX, RGB, HSL and OKLCH and check accessibility contrast (WCAG).
color-converter.about: The color converter reads a color in HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH or by its CSS name and shows it in all of those formats, ready to copy into your CSS or design tool. It also calculates the color's contrast on a background following the WCAG 2 guidelines and tells you whether it meets AA and AAA for normal and large text, so your text stays readable.

faq.q1: What is OKLCH for?
faq.a1: It describes colors by lightness, chroma and hue in a way that matches how we perceive them. It makes harmonious palettes easier, and every modern browser accepts it in CSS.
faq.q2: How much contrast does text need?
faq.a2: Level AA asks for at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; level AAA, 7:1 and 4.5:1.
faq.q3: Does it accept transparent colors?
faq.a3: Yes: #RRGGBBAA, rgb(… / 0.5) and similar. For contrast, the color is blended with the background the way a browser would.

unit-converter.title: Unit converter
unit-converter.description: Convert length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, data and time between metric and imperial units.
unit-converter.about: The unit converter instantly converts a value between metric, imperial and US units: length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, data size and time. It uses exact definitions (1 inch = 2.54 cm, 1 pound = 453.59237 g) and shows the value in every unit at once. Both decimal points and decimal commas are accepted.

faq.q1: Are cups and gallons US or UK measures?
faq.a1: Teaspoons, tablespoons, cups, pints, quarts and gallons are US customary measures; the British imperial gallon is listed separately.
faq.a2: With SI prefixes, 1 GB = 1000 MB. Operating systems sometimes count in powers of 2: those are GiB and MiB, which you can convert too.
faq.q3: How precise are the results?
faq.a3: Up to 10 significant digits are shown. The equivalences are exact by definition; the number is only rounded for display.

compress-image.title: Compress image
compress-image.description: Shrink JPG, PNG, WEBP and AVIF photos, or fit them under an exact file size for a form.
compress-image.about: Compress image re-encodes your photos so they take less space without changing their pixel size. Pick a level (low, recommended or strong) or an exact maximum size, like the 100 KB or 200 KB many online forms ask for: we find the best quality that fits and, if that is not enough, scale the image down. PNG files are optimized losslessly at the low level and reduced to a color palette at the others. You can also switch to WEBP or AVIF, which are smaller at the same quality. Everything happens in your browser, and metadata (such as GPS location) is removed.

faq.q1: How much smaller will my photo get?
faq.a1: It depends on the photo: a phone JPG usually drops 40% to 80% at the recommended level. If the image was already optimized and can't get smaller, you get the original back unchanged.
faq.q2: How do I get a photo under 100 KB for a form?
faq.a2: Choose “Exact file size” and the 100 KB button (or type another size). The result is at most that size; if needed its pixel size is reduced too, and we tell you by how much.
faq.q3: Why was my PNG saved as JPG?
faq.a3: In exact-size mode PNG files are saved as JPG, because PNG has no quality setting. If your PNG has transparency, choose WEBP to keep it.
faq.a4: With JPG, WEBP and AVIF, a little: the low level is barely noticeable and the strong level favors size. PNG at the low level loses nothing.

resize-image.title: Resize image
resize-image.description: Change the size of your images in pixels, by percentage or to each social network's dimensions.
resize-image.about: Resize image changes the width and height of your photos: type the pixels you want (keeping the proportions or not), a percentage, or pick a ready-made social media size such as an Instagram square post, a story or a YouTube thumbnail. When the proportions don't match, you can crop the edges or add borders so nothing of the photo is lost. It works with JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, in batches, and you can change the format at the same time. Everything is processed in your browser.

faq.q1: Is an image smaller than the requested size enlarged?
faq.a1: In pixel mode with proportions, no, unless you tick “Allow enlarging smaller images”, since enlarging adds no detail. Social media sizes do enlarge it to fill the format.
faq.q2: What if the photo doesn't have the social network's proportions?
faq.a2: “Crop the edges” keeps the center of the photo and crops what doesn't fit. “Add borders” fits the whole photo and fills the sides (white for JPG, transparent for PNG, WEBP and AVIF).
faq.q3: Is there a maximum size?
faq.a3: The result can have up to about 36 megapixels (for example 6928 × 5196); larger requests are scaled down keeping the shape. Each file can be up to 50 MB.
faq.q4: Does it work with animated GIFs?
faq.a4: Only the first frame is resized. A video-to-GIF tool for animated GIFs will come later.

rotate-image.title: Rotate image
rotate-image.description: Turn your photos 90° or 180° and mirror them, in batches.
rotate-image.about: Rotate image turns your photos 90° right, 90° left or 180°, and can also mirror them (horizontal flip) or turn them upside down (vertical flip). The orientation saved by the camera is applied first, so the result is exactly what you see on screen and looks the same in every app. It works with JPG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, TIFF and HEIC, in batches, and keeps the format (HEIC is saved as JPG). Everything is processed in your browser.

faq.q1: My photo looks fine on my phone but sideways on my computer. Does this help?
faq.a1: Yes. Choose “Just straighten”: the orientation saved by the camera is applied and the photo stays upright in every app, without turning it further.
faq.q2: Do I lose quality when rotating?
faq.a2: PNG, BMP, TIFF and GIF lose nothing. JPG, WEBP and AVIF are saved again at high quality (92), a difference you won't notice in practice.
faq.q3: Can I rotate and flip at the same time?
faq.a3: Yes: the image is rotated first and flipped after. For example, 90° right with a horizontal flip.
faq.a4: No: saving the rotated image removes the metadata, including GPS location. To remove metadata without touching the image, use “Remove EXIF metadata”.

remove-exif.title: Remove EXIF metadata
remove-exif.description: Erase GPS location, camera and date from your photos without losing quality.
remove-exif.about: Remove EXIF metadata erases the information you can't see but that travels with the file: the GPS location where the photo was taken, the camera or phone make and model, the date and time, the software used and the author. Before erasing, we show you what each photo contained. For JPG, PNG and WEBP the image is not compressed again: the same image data is copied without the metadata, so quality is identical. JPGs keep only their orientation, so the photo doesn't show sideways, and their color profile. HEIC files are saved as JPG without metadata. Everything happens in your browser.

faq.q1: Why remove metadata before sharing a photo?
faq.a1: A phone photo can carry the exact coordinates of your home or workplace. Many social networks remove them, but email, chat attachments and cloud links usually send the original file.
faq.a2: Not for JPG, PNG or WEBP: the image data is copied byte for byte. Only HEIC files are saved again, as high-quality JPG.
faq.q3: What is kept?
faq.a3: What's needed to display the photo correctly: the orientation (JPG) and the color profile. GPS, camera, dates, software, author, thumbnails, XMP, IPTC and comments are removed.
faq.q4: How do I check the location is gone?
faq.a4: Run the clean photo through this tool again: it should say it found no metadata. You can also check the file's properties on your computer.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Privacy is at the core of Fileflect. This page explains what data we handle, why, and for how long.

sections.heading: Files processed on your device
sections.body: Images and PDFs you convert, compress, merge, split or reorder are processed inside your browser. Those files are never sent to our servers and we have no access to them.

sections.heading: Files processed on our server
sections.body: Office documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, RTF, TXT), PDF to Word and, only when your browser can't do it, some images are processed on our server over an encrypted connection. They are processed in memory or temporary storage and deleted within 1 hour at most. We don't look at them, share them or use them for anything else.

sections.heading: Data we store
sections.body: For each conversion we only store metadata: input and output format, size, date, whether it ran in the browser or on the server and, if you are signed in, your user. Never the file's name or content. If you create an account we store your email (and your name and picture if you sign in with Google) and your subscription status.

sections.heading: Payments
sections.body: Pro payments are processed by Mercado Pago (or another payment provider in some countries). We never receive or store your card details; only the subscription id and status.

sections.heading: Cookies and local storage
sections.body: We use necessary cookies to remember your language, your country for pricing and your session, and local storage for the light or dark theme. Free-plan users see Google AdSense ads, which may use their own cookies; you can manage them in Google's ad settings.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask to access, correct or delete your data and your account through the contact page. Cancelling a subscription doesn't delete the account; if you want it deleted, ask us and we will.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By using Fileflect you accept these terms. They are written to be clear; if anything is unclear, write to us.

sections.heading: The service
sections.body: Fileflect converts, compresses and organizes files. Basic features are free and need no account. The Pro plan raises limits and removes ads.

sections.heading: Your files
sections.body: Your files remain yours. Only upload or process files you have the right to use. We claim no rights over them.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body: Don't use Fileflect for illegal activities, to send malware or to overload the service (for example with massive automated uploads). We may limit usage to protect the service.

sections.heading: Pro subscription
sections.body: Pro is billed in advance, monthly or yearly, in local currency where available. You can cancel anytime from My account: it won't renew and you keep Pro until the end of the paid period.

sections.heading: No warranty
sections.body: We do our best to make conversions accurate, but the service is provided “as is”. Some complex formats may not convert perfectly; always keep your original files.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: We may update these terms. If a change is important, we'll announce it on the site.
